prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

The present patent provides a method for improving the construction process of a wide-base radial truck tire, and the improvement of the tire construction process is realized by the design of carcass ply, the tire belt drum and the tire semi-finished components. The patent solves the problem of carcass bending, and provides theoretical guidance and technical support for improving the performance of wide-angle radial tires. The design method of the belt drum of the tire molding machine effectively controls the cords elongation of the belt. In addition, the problem of uneven force in the cords of the belt is eliminated, which dispels the abnormal flow of the wide-base tire shoulder rubber to the center of the crown during the shaping process, thus improving the durability and operability of the tire. The proposed semi-finished components design method in this patent can accurately design the tire semi-finished parts material distribution map, significantly improve the finished tire and the theoretical design of tire material distribution consistency, thus reducing tire development cycle and development costs.

outputs.L1:
The present patent provides a method for improving the construction process of wide-base radial truck tires through the design of the carcass ply, tire belt drum, and semi-finished tire components. The patent addresses the issue of carcass bending and provides theoretical guidance and technical support for enhancing the performance of wide-angle radial tires.

The proposed design method for the belt drum of the tire-building machine effectively controls belt-cord elongation and eliminates uneven forces in the belt cords. This prevents the abnormal flow of shoulder rubber toward the center of the crown during the shaping of wide-base tires, thereby improving tire durability and handling performance.

Furthermore, the method proposed in this patent for designing semi-finished components enables the accurate preparation of material distribution maps for semi-finished tire components. It significantly improves the consistency between the material distribution of the finished tire and the theoretical design, thereby shortening the tire development cycle and reducing development costs.
outputs.L2: This patent describes an improved manufacturing process for wide-base radial truck tires through optimized designs for the carcass ply, belt drum, and semi-finished tire components. The disclosed approach addresses carcass bending and offers theoretical and technical guidance for enhancing wide-angle radial tire performance. The belt-drum design for the tire-building machine effectively regulates belt-cord elongation and ensures a more uniform distribution of force among the cords. This prevents abnormal movement of shoulder rubber toward the center of the tread crown during shaping, thereby improving tire durability and handling. The patent also introduces a method for designing semi-finished components that enables accurate preparation of material-distribution maps. By bringing the finished tire’s material distribution into closer alignment with the theoretical design, this method substantially shortens development time and lowers development costs.
outputs.L3:
The patent introduces an improved construction process for wide-base radial truck tires by redesigning key elements, including the carcass plies, belt drum, and semi-finished components. These changes address common manufacturing challenges associated with wide-base tire structures and provide practical technical guidance for improving overall tire performance.

A major benefit of the method is its ability to reduce carcass bending during tire shaping and assembly. By improving the geometry and behavior of the carcass plies, the process promotes a more stable and consistent tire structure. The redesigned belt drum also controls belt-cord elongation more effectively, ensuring that loads are distributed evenly among the cords rather than concentrated in specific areas.

This more uniform cord-force distribution helps prevent abnormal movement of shoulder rubber toward the center of the crown during shaping. As a result, the finished tire maintains a more accurate profile and balanced internal structure, which can enhance durability, handling stability, and service performance.

In addition, the patent provides an improved design method for semi-finished components. By increasing the accuracy of material placement and distribution, the method reduces the need for repeated design adjustments and physical trials. This can shorten tire-development cycles, lower development costs, and improve manufacturing consistency.
outputs.L4:
The patent relates to the design and manufacture of wide-base radial truck tires, particularly tires intended to carry heavy loads while maintaining durability, stability, and predictable handling. Conventional manufacturing methods can cause the carcass ply to bend or shift during shaping, while belt cords may experience uneven elongation and tension. In addition, rubber can flow abnormally near the shoulder regions during molding and vulcanization. These effects can cause the material distribution in the finished tire to differ from the theoretical design, reducing structural uniformity and making performance more difficult to predict.

To address these problems, the patent redesigns the carcass ply, the belt-building drum, and the relevant semi-finished components as an integrated system. The carcass ply is configured so that its position and contour after shaping more closely match the intended profile of the finished tire. The belt drum is also designed to control the placement and deformation of the belt layers during assembly. Together, these changes reduce unwanted carcass bending and limit irregular changes in belt-cord length.

The manufacturing method further controls the dimensions, profiles, and positioning of semi-finished rubber components before the tire is molded. Particular attention is given to the shoulder area, where material is especially susceptible to displacement under pressure. By matching the geometry of the uncured components to the deformation expected during building and vulcanization, the process prevents excessive or uneven shoulder-rubber flow and preserves the intended thickness distribution.

Another important feature is the equalization of forces acting on the belt cords. More uniform cord elongation and tension help maintain a stable belt contour and reduce local stress concentrations. As a result, the belt package and carcass cooperate more effectively under load, improving resistance to fatigue, separation, irregular wear, and other failures associated with heavy-duty service.

The resulting finished tire has a material distribution that more closely corresponds to the theoretical design established during development. This improves dimensional accuracy, structural consistency, durability, and handling performance. It also reduces reliance on repeated trial production, section analysis, and design correction. The patented approach therefore shortens the tire-development cycle, lowers tooling and testing costs, improves manufacturing efficiency, and supports more reliable production of wide-base radial truck tires.

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain in formal patent-summary language how the disclosed tire molding process addresses uneven belt-cord forces and improves consistency between theoretical and finished-tire material distributions.
counterfactuals.output:
The disclosed tire-molding process compensates for nonuniform forces generated in the belt cords during shaping and vulcanization. In particular, the process establishes the geometry and material placement of the green tire in consideration of variations in cord tension arising across the belt width, rather than assuming uniform radial displacement of the belt assembly. The belt and adjacent rubber components are thereby positioned or shaped so that deformation occurring upon expansion against the molding surface is controlled and distributed in accordance with the intended finished-tire profile.

By accounting in advance for belt-cord restraint and the resulting differential movement of the tread, shoulder, and sidewall regions, the process suppresses localized displacement, rubber flow, and thickness variation during molding. Consequently, the positions and cross-sectional distributions of the constituent materials in the vulcanized tire more closely correspond to those prescribed by the theoretical tire design. The process thus reduces product-to-product variation, improves dimensional and structural uniformity, and permits the designed performance characteristics to be reproduced more reliably in the finished tire.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
